answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may influence a market or claim rewards. A reputation score then grows only from interactions with independently staked participants, so splitting one history across many names does not multiply trust. An attacker must tie up real capital in every sybil and risks losing it when identities coordinate to manipulate outcomes. Calling a stake glacier, copper, or zephyr changes nothing: the deterrent is the opportunity cost and slash risk, not the label.
